# Wrist-flick pulse recognizer: evidence (2026-11-02)

> Part of the [Arooma design brain](../../design/README.md). Spec: [wrist-flick pulse recognizer](../../design/specs/2026-11-02-wrist-flick-pulse-recognizer.md). Research: [reference.md](../../../reference.md).

**All measurements here are synthetic.** They come from deterministic traces generated by `ios/Tests/GyroFlip/Corpus.swift` and replayed through both recognizers. No physical iPhone was used, and every physical target is NOT RUN. The owner-calibration procedure in the spec produces the physical evidence.

## Files

- `gyro-tests-output.txt`: full output of the test runner on this branch, including the A/B comparison for development seeds (1…) and held-out seeds (9000…). Reproduce with the command in `ios/Tests/GyroFlip/main.swift`.

## Test results

- 192 checks passed, 0 failed. 141 are the PR #43 classifier checks, unchanged. 51 are new: pulse-recognizer rejections, valid flicks in both axes and at five grip angles, rebound, cooldown, latency, dropouts and suppression, the corpus gates on development seeds, and the trace-file codec.
- Corpus gates (development seeds): zero double flips, zero wrong directions, flicks of 0.7 rad and above recognized at least 95%, p95 latency at most 250 ms, at most 1 accidental flip per 100 ordinary trials.

## Baseline versus new, synthetic

See the spec's "Synthetic measurements" section for the table. In short:

| | PR #43 | Pulse |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wrong direction (development / held-out, of 400) | 17 / 22 | 0 / 0 |
| Double flips | 0 | 0 |
| Accidental flips, 600 ordinary trials (dev / held-out) | 1 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Latency p95 (dev / held-out) | 165 / 172 ms | 221 / 220 ms |

## Not run

- Physical iPhone recognition, double flips, accidental flips during browsing, latency, holographic continuity, Off and Reduce Motion behavior on device.
- Trace files from a real device. The owner's calibration session produces them.
